effect_estimate.comment: Purely qualitative study documenting the co-creation and stakeholder self-evaluation of an informal social accountability mechanism process; no quantitative effect estimates or statistical tests are reported.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Childcare center managers and parents co-created a four-step informal social accountability mechanism (iSAM) process to improve childcare WASH service delivery—(1) defining accountability to whom and for what, (2) performing actions and sharing information (fee payments and providing WASH amenities), (3) judging and assessing performance (via center visits, shared photos, and written/phone reports), and (4) learning and adapting (rewards, installment payment accommodations, or child exclusion sanctions for non-compliance)—which participants self-evaluated as enhancing mutual understanding, inclusion, ownership, contextual fit, and perceived WASH service delivery, while constrained by time burdens, leadership needs, inconsistent stakeholder commitment, and parents' financial inability to pay fees or purchase WASH supplies.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 6, Table 2; PDF pp. 7–11, Results

mechanism_certainty.comment: Qualitative design ceiling is 2 under CODEBOOK.md §9. Rated 2 because the study directly documents through primary empirical accounts of childcare managers and parents how participatory co-creation, informal social accountability, fee obligations, installment accommodations, performance monitoring/reporting, and exclusion sanctions operate on WASH provision and access in informal-settlement childcare centers.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines participatory co-creation of informal social accountability mechanisms between parents and childcare center managers (participation), parental WASH fee obligations and time/procedural burdens of multi-step co-creation (BURDEN, fees, procedural_steps), contextual tailoring and installment payment flexibility for non-compliant parents (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, accommodation), and monitoring/reporting with rewards or child exclusion for non-compliance (ENFORCEMENT, sanction).

mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 6, Table 2; PDF pp. 7–11, Results

sample_size.comment: Total N = 200 purposively sampled participants (68 childcare center managers and 132 parents across Korogocho and Viwandani), engaged between December 2021 and May 2022 in 24 formative FGDs (8–10 participants per FGD; 8 parent FGDs and 4 manager FGDs per site) and 4 participatory workshops (~50 participants per workshop) followed by post-workshop reflection FGDs.
sample_size.value: 200 participants across 2 informal settlements (100 per settlement: 34 childcare center managers/owners and 66 parents of children under 5 years in Korogocho, and 34 childcare center managers/owners and 66 parents in Viwandani), participating in 24 formative focus group discussions (12 per site) and 4 participatory workshops (2 per site, ~50 participants each) with post-workshop reflection FGDs
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 5, Target population, sampling and sample size, Table 1, and Data collection process; PDF p. 6, Results

study_design.comment: Primary qualitative and collaborative participatory study reported per COREQ criteria, combining formative FGDs, stakeholder co-creation workshops, and post-workshop reflection FGDs analyzed in NVivo 12 using framework analysis informed by Coleman's social capital framework.
study_design.value: Qualitative participatory study using focus group discussions (FGDs) and stakeholder participatory workshops with framework analysis

evidence_quotes.quote: © 2023 Chumo, Kabaria, Elsey, Ozano, Phillips-Howard and Mberu. This is an open-access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY).

This study explored the co-creation process of iSAMs for WASH service delivery in childcare centers in two informal settlements in Nairobi, Kenya, and the self-evaluation of the process using FGDs and workshops.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 5, Target population, sampling and sample size
evidence_quotes.quote: We sampled 100 participants comprising 34 childcare center owners catering to children under-5 years and 66 parents of children under-5 years attending the childcare centers in each of the two study sites.
In total 200 participants took part in our study, comprising childcare managers and parents (see Table 1) in the Methods section.
This was a qualitative study, using focus group discussions (FGDs) and stakeholder participatory workshops.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 9, Step four: Learning and adapting informal social accountability mechanisms
evidence_quotes.quote: For parents who are not compliant with what we agreed, it is good to communicate with them, encourage and train them to pay in instalments for their children to access WASH facilities. However, when they cannot improve in their compliance, we do not allow them to bring their children to the centre
